newsitem.title: USA: Public Storage forms venture with fund.
newsitem.headline: Public Storage forms venture with fund.

text.p: Public Storage Inc said it has formed an off balance sheet equity joint venture with a major state pension fund to develop up to $220 million of self-storage properties nationwide.
The real estate investment trust said the venture is expected to develop between 50 and 60 new self-storage facilities over the next three years.
It said this represents one of the largest development programs implemented by a REIT to date.
In the transaction, the pension fund will contribute approximately 70 percent, or $154 million, of the total capital to the venture, with Public Storage contributing the $66 million balance.
Public Storage did not identify the pension fund and the information was not immediately available.

Public Storage said the venture was structured off balance sheet to allow the company to expand its operations while not incurring the dilution of earnings that typically results from the construction and lease-up of new properties.
In addition, Public Storage said it would seed the joint venture with up to 25 existing properties, which are currently in various stages of development.
Additional properties will be contributed to the venture once they are identified for development, the company said.
Public Storage will ultimately have the right to purchase the pension fund's interest in all the developed properties upon stabilization.
BT Securities Corporation, through its real estate investment banking group, structured the venture and advised Public Storage.
Heitman Capital Management Corporation, a Chicago-based institutional real estate advisor, represented the pension fund.
Public Storage said it is the largest owner and operator of self-storage facilities in the United States, with 1,108 properties in 37 states, and one of the nation's five largest REITs.
